guidance.statement: Targeting crude steel production of 22.5 million tons for FY27.
Capex guidance for FY27 is INR15,000 crores.
FY27 capex target of ₹15,000 Cr, rising to over ₹20,000 Cr next year and ₹25,000-26,000 Cr thereafter
Full-year sales volume maintained with growth over FY26
Q2 NSR expected ₹1,000-2,000/t below Q1 on monsoon demand
Imported coal cost expected to fall ₹1,000-1,500/t in Q2 versus Q1
Cost reduction of ₹2,000-3,000/t targeted this year; ₹2,000/t net from IISCO expansion by FY29

industry: Commodities > Metals & Mining > Ferrous Metals > Iron & Steel

operating_notes.text: Q4FY26 average NSR for long products was INR53,400 and flat was INR51,000 per ton.
Q1FY27 NSR was ₹57,100/t (flat ₹57,200, long ₹57,100); July NSR averaged ₹55,600/t.
Imported coal cost ₹21,300/t in Q1 versus ₹18,100/t in Q4FY26; captive coal expected at ₹5,000-6,000/t from Tasra in December.
Iron-ore sales from captive mines were 1.1 mt in Q1 (₹574 Cr turnover, ~₹150 Cr EBITDA) against 0.31 mt a year ago; FY27 target 8 mt.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹30,813.49 Cr (+5.1% YoY), net profit ₹1,835.47 Cr (+46.7% YoY).
Steel Authority of India reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹110,810 Cr and net profit of ₹3,233 Cr.

Steel Authority of India Limited’s Management, led by ED (F&A) & Company Secretary M.B.Balakrishnan, held a conference call on 16 May 2026 discussing Q4FY26 & FY26 results with analysts and investors.
Steel Authority of India reported Q4 FY26 transcript highlights, guiding for FY27 crude steel volume of 22.5 MnT and ₹15,000 Cr capex.
On its 28 July 2026 Q1FY27 call, SAIL reported EBITDA of ₹4,356 Cr (up over 50% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,636 Cr, with debt-equity at 0.36 and FY27 capex guided at ₹15,000 Cr.
